description: IoT Village highlights embedded firmware analysis, smart home and industrial IoT security, reverse supply chain hardware trojans, silicon RNG entropy, and connected device policy.

talks.title: I Used AppSec Skills to Hack IoT and So Can You
talks.teaser: Alexi Kojenov demonstrates applying core web application security skills to audit embedded Linux IoT devices, finding critical firmware and web UI flaws.
talks.summary:
Bridging Application Security and Embedded IoT

While AppSec and IoT are often viewed as distinct disciplines, modern embedded IoT devices are essentially lightweight Linux computers running web servers, daemons, and APIs.

Extracting and Auditing Embedded Web Applications

Alexi Kojenov demonstrates extracting firmware root filesystems using Binwalk to inspect backend PHP, CGI, and JavaScript source code directly.

Exploiting Classic Web Flaws in Embedded Environments

Kojenov walks through identifying command injection, path traversal, and broken authentication across embedded web interfaces, popping root shells on target devices.

A Guide for Web AppSec Professionals Transitioning to IoT

The author provides a methodology for traditional web penetration testers to apply their skills to hardware and firmware security assessments.

talks.title: 1.21 Gigawatts: Vulnerabilities in Solar Panels
talks.teaser: Waylon Grange analyzes the security posture of smart solar power inverters, demonstrating hardware probing, firmware extraction, and remote takeover vectors.
talks.summary:
The Expanding Footprint of Connected Solar Infrastructure

As renewable energy adoption accelerates, smart photovoltaic solar inverters with IoT cloud connectivity are deployed across residential rooftops and commercial solar farms.

Hardware Teardown and Debug Port Interrogation

Waylon Grange inspects leading solar inverter hardware, tapping UART serial headers and SPI flash chips to extract underlying embedded Linux firmware.

Uncovering Critical Inverter Vulnerabilities

Auditing proprietary monitoring protocols and firmware binaries reveals unauthenticated debug daemons, hardcoded credentials, and cloud API authorization flaws.

Mitigating Systemic Grid Disruption Risks

The author explores how mass remote shutdown of distributed solar inverters could destabilize the electrical grid, proposing firmware hardening and network isolation controls.

talks.title: LED Light Lunacy: Hacking Connected Smart Lights
talks.teaser: Victor Hanna reverse engineers smart LED light controller protocols during lockdown, demonstrating unauthorized local and wireless lighting takeover.
talks.summary:
Victor Hanna (glyph) details an entertaining and technically illuminating security research journey into cloud-connected IoT devices, demonstrating how a lockdown project investigating smart LED strip lights exposed systemic authorization flaws across millions of connected lights worldwide.

[06:40] Hanna analyzes the architecture of inexpensive Wi-Fi LED controllers (such as Magic Home / Flux LED devices), examining the communications between local microcontrollers, mobile companion apps, and central cloud infrastructure. He walks through reverse engineering the Android application, analyzing local UDP broadcast discovery packets, and proxying HTTP/REST API traffic through Burp Suite.

[13:48] The presentation reveals severe cloud-side security vulnerabilities, specifically broken object-level authorization (BOLA) and insecure direct object references (IDOR). By inspecting authentication tokens and account identifiers, Hanna discovered that the cloud API failed to validate device ownership. He demonstrates forging API requests [21:14] to enumerate device IDs globally, allowing him to query device statuses, leak user registration details, and remotely turn off or manipulate the lighting colors of smart bulbs and LED strips across the world. The talk concludes with disclosure challenges and guidance on securing IoT APIs.

(AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: IoT Testing Crash Course
talks.teaser: Tim Jensen (EapolSniper) delivers a hands-on crash course on IoT penetration testing, covering network discovery, firmware extraction, and binwalk analysis.
talks.summary:
Foundational Skills for IoT Vulnerability Assessment

Assessing embedded IoT devices requires combining network reconnaissance, hardware teardown, firmware extraction, and binary reverse engineering.

Extracting and Analyzing Firmware with Binwalk

Tim Jensen walks through dumping SPI flash memory chips, downloading vendor firmware updates, and unpacking filesystem images with Binwalk.

Auditing Embedded Binaries and Network Daemons

Jensen demonstrates identifying vulnerable CGI scripts, hardcoded backdoor accounts, and unencrypted management daemons running on embedded Linux systems.

Practical Lab Setup and Tooling Recommendations

The presentation provides aspiring hardware hackers with a budget-friendly hardware toolkit and structured methodology for analyzing consumer smart devices.

talks.title: When Penetration Testing Isn't Penetration Testing at All
talks.teaser: Ted Harrington challenges industry misconceptions around penetration testing, contrasting commoditized vulnerability scans with true adversarial assessments.
talks.summary:
The Misuse of the Penetration Testing Label

The term 'penetration testing' is frequently commoditized across the security industry, with automated vulnerability scanner reports marketed as comprehensive security assessments.

Vulnerability Scanning vs. True Adversarial Penetration Testing

Ted Harrington distinguishes surface-level compliance scans from deep, threat-modeled penetration tests that chain complex logic flaws across IoT ecosystems.

Threat Modeling Connected Hardware Systems

Harrington outlines the essential phases of effective IoT testing—including attack surface mapping, threat modeling, exploit development, and root-cause analysis.

Building Resilient Security Testing Programs

The presentation provides enterprise buyers and product developers with practical guidelines to evaluate security vendors and demand high-impact testing.

talks.title: IoT Devices as Government Witnesses: Surveillance & Digital Evidence
talks.teaser: Stephen Sessler and Matt Hendricks examine how law enforcement uses consumer IoT data (Fitbits, Amazon Echos, smart appliances) as courtroom evidence.
talks.summary:
Consumer IoT Devices in Criminal Investigations

From Fitbits implicating murder suspects to Amazon Echo audio recordings subpoenaed by prosecutors, smart consumer devices increasingly serve as digital witnesses in courtrooms.

Law Enforcement Surveillance and Protest Monitoring

Stephen Sessler and Matt Hendricks detail documented cases where police and federal agencies subpoenaed vehicle telemetry, smart TV logs, and smart refrigerator sensors.

Fourth Amendment Protections and the Third-Party Doctrine

The authors analyze the constitutional friction between Fourth Amendment search protections and the Third-Party Doctrine governing data stored on commercial cloud platforms.

Technical Defenses and Privacy Recommendations

The presentation provides citizens and developers with practical privacy guidelines, including local storage architectures, end-to-end encryption, and telemetry opting-out.

talks.title: MIPS-X: The Next IoT Frontier in Emulation & Vulnerability Research
talks.teaser: Michael Ross and Nick Balazs present techniques for emulating non-standard MIPS architectures in QEMU to accelerate dynamic IoT firmware analysis.
talks.summary:
The Complexity of Dynamic IoT Firmware Analysis

Dynamic vulnerability research on embedded devices requires emulating target binaries and network daemons without access to physical developer boards.

Overcoming MIPS Emulation Bottlenecks in QEMU

Michael Ross and Nick Balazs investigate emulation hurdles encountered with legacy and proprietary MIPS-X chipsets commonly found in routers and IP cameras.

Customizing Buildroot and Hardware Peripheral Stubs

The authors demonstrate developing custom NVRAM stubs, mock peripheral drivers, and QEMU patches to achieve stable system-level firmware emulation.

Automating Zero-Day Discovery via Dynamic Fuzzing

Ross and Balazs showcase dynamic fuzzing workflows on emulated MIPS targets, discovering unauthenticated memory corruption flaws in embedded web services.

talks.title: Ethics at the Edge: Trust, Sensing, & Actuation in Smart Devices
talks.teaser: Intel AI architect Ria Cheruvu explores the ethical and security challenges of intelligent edge IoT devices performing real-time sensing and physical actuation.
talks.summary:
The Proliferation of Intelligent Edge Devices

Modern IoT devices increasingly embed computer vision, natural language processing, and automated actuation, interacting dynamically with physical environments.

Redefining Trusted Entities in Pervasive Surveillance

Ria Cheruvu examines incidents like the 2021 Verkada camera hack, illustrating the extreme risks when centralized cloud platforms manage thousands of edge sensors.

Ethical Dilemmas in Autonomous Actuation and Sensing

Cheruvu explores the safety, privacy, and accountability implications of edge devices making autonomous decisions affecting human subjects without consent.

A Governance Framework for Trustworthy Edge Computing

The author proposes transparent design principles, local data processing guardrails, and cryptographic attestation standards for intelligent IoT devices.

talks.title: You're Doing IoT RNG Wrong: Cryptographic Entropy in Silicon
talks.teaser: Dan Petro and Allan Cecil uncover systemic flaws in hardware Random Number Generators across IoT chipsets, leading to static zero-value encryption keys.
talks.summary:
The Hidden Flaws in Embedded Cryptographic Randomness

Cryptographic protocols on IoT devices—such as TLS key exchanges and AES encryption—depend entirely on hardware Random Number Generators (RNG) for secrecy.

Auditing Hardware RNG Implementations Across Silicon Vendors

Dan Petro and Allan Cecil audit hardware datasheets and driver libraries from leading IoT microcontroller vendors, uncovering dangerous software integration flaws.

Extracting Static and Zero-Entropy Keys in Production Devices

The authors demonstrate real-world devices where uninitialized RNG hardware registers resulted in devices encrypting traffic with fixed zero-keys.

Verified Best Practices for Secure Embedded Randomness

Petro and Cecil provide developers with verified guidelines for combining hardware jitter entropy with cryptographic pseudo-random number generators (PRNGs).

talks.title: Representation Matters: Moving Beyond Lip Service in Tech DEI
talks.teaser: Chloe Messdaghi and Farah Eddy address systemic barriers facing marginalized communities in cybersecurity, sharing actionable frameworks for genuine inclusion.
talks.summary:
The Reality Behind Corporate Diversity Initiatives

While technology companies frequently promote Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) publicly, marginalized professionals continue to experience systemic exclusion behind the scenes.

First-Hand Accounts from Marginalized Professionals

Chloe Messdaghi and Farah Eddy share real-world stories of workplace bias, compensation disparities, and promotional barriers in infosec.

Exposing Performative Corporate Lip Service

The speakers examine common pitfalls where organizations implement superficial DEI programs without addressing toxic workplace cultures or leadership accountability.

Actionable Blueprints for True Inclusion and Equity

Messdaghi and Eddy present practical retention strategies, pay transparency policies, and mentorship initiatives to build genuinely inclusive security organizations.

talks.title: BLUEMONDAY Series: Exploitation and Mapping of Vulnerable Devices
talks.teaser: Ken Pyle presents the BLUEMONDAY research series, uncovering systemic insecure-by-design vulnerabilities in enterprise IoT, NAS, and cloud gateways.
talks.summary:
Insecure Design in Enterprise IoT Gateways

Enterprise backup appliances, NAS devices, and cloud-managed network gateways (such as Datto, Meraki, and Synology) manage vast repositories of sensitive corporate data.

The BLUEMONDAY Vulnerability Research Findings

Ken Pyle discloses a series of architectural design flaws and web application vulnerabilities that allow attackers to bypass authentication and access device shares.

Exploiting Self-Provisioning Cloud Relay Services

Pyle illustrates how automated cloud relay connections inadvertently expose internal storage volumes and administrative interfaces to public internet scanning.

Remediation Guidance for Enterprise Deployments

The author provides network administrators with segmentation rules and configuration audits to protect corporate storage gateways from unauthorized remote access.

talks.title: Strategic Trust and Deception in the Internet of Things
talks.teaser: Juneau Jones applies game theory to IoT ecosystems, modeling dynamic trust relationships, honey-tokens, and strategic deception between smart devices.
talks.summary:
Modeling IoT Interactions Through Game Theory

Game theory offers powerful mathematical models for analyzing strategic choices, payoffs, and deception between autonomous devices and threat actors.

Trust Relationships and Asymmetric Information in IoT Networks

Juneau Jones analyzes how smart devices establish trust and verify peer device identities across open wireless and local network protocols.

Deploying Deception Mechanisms to Alter Attacker Payoffs

By introducing deceptive endpoints, honey-services, and artificial latency, defenders increase the cost of adversary reconnaissance across IoT deployments.

Optimizing Multi-Device Defense Strategies

Jones provides a mathematical framework for deploying deception networks that dynamically adapt based on detected adversary probing.

talks.title: 5 Years of IoT Vulnerability Research and Countless 0-Days
talks.teaser: Jay Balan shares insights from five years of IoT vulnerability research, demonstrating authentication bypasses, root shells, and practical disclosure lessons.
talks.summary:
Reflecting on Five Years of IoT Vulnerability Research

Over half a decade of auditing connected consumer and enterprise IoT hardware reveals persistent, repeating classes of security flaws across product generations.

Demonstrating Real-World 0-Day Exploit Chains

Jay Balan walks through multiple live exploit demonstrations—including pre-authentication memory corruption, hidden debug APIs, and cryptographic bypasses.

Why Old Vulnerabilities Refuse to Die in IoT

Balan analyzes the commercial dynamics and supply chain pressures that cause vendors to repeatedly clone unpatched legacy codebases into new device models.

A Roadmap for Getting Started in Hardware Research

The presentation provides aspiring vulnerability researchers with essential lab tooling, static analysis workflows, and coordinated disclosure strategies.

talks.title: Alexa, Have You Been Compromised? Hacking Smart Voice Assistants
talks.teaser: Hutch investigates the corporate and domestic attack surface of voice assistants like Amazon Alexa, demonstrating skill hijacking and acoustic command injection.
talks.summary:
The Expansion of Voice Assistants into Workplaces

Smart voice assistants (such as Amazon Alexa and Google Assistant) are increasingly deployed in corporate conference rooms and smart offices, listening to sensitive conversations.

Threat Modeling Connected Smart Speakers

Hutch analyzes the multi-layered attack surface of voice assistants—including companion mobile apps, third-party skills, and acoustic physical channels.

Exploiting Malicious Voice Skills and Network Interfaces

The author demonstrates practical exploitation vectors, such as malicious Alexa skill name squatting and local network command injection.

Securing Voice Technologies in Enterprise Environments

The presentation provides enterprise security teams with deployment policies, network isolation guidelines, and physical microphone mute verification.

talks.title: Defending IoT in the Future of High-Tech Warfare
talks.teaser: Harshit Agrawal evaluates RF-based attacks and electronic warfare tactics targeting military and critical infrastructure Internet of Things networks.
talks.summary:
The Weaponization of IoT in Modern Geopolitical Conflict

Connected sensors and automated edge devices play a growing role in battlefield logistics, surveillance, and critical civilian infrastructure.

Evaluating RF Attack Surfaces and Wireless Disruption

Harshit Agrawal reviews practical RF attack vectors against IoT protocols (Zigbee, LoRaWAN, cellular), covering packet injection, jamming, and signal spoofing.

Modeling the Impact of Mass IoT Disruption

The author analyzes how coordinated electronic warfare against commercial and tactical IoT networks can blind defenders and paralyze command infrastructure.

Architecting Resilient Wireless IoT Defenses

Agrawal provides strategic defense recommendations, including frequency hopping, protocol encryption, and out-of-band telemetry verification.

talks.title: Reverse Supply Chain Attack: Weaponizing the Return Merchandise Pipeline
talks.teaser: Claroty researchers introduce the reverse supply chain attack vector, showing how returned merchandise (RMA) can be trojanized to infiltrate manufacturers.
talks.summary:
Expanding Beyond Upstream Supply Chain Threats

While standard supply chain security focuses on components traveling from supplier to customer, the reverse logistics pipeline (RMA and product returns) represents an overlooked vector.

Introducing the Reverse Supply Chain Attack Concept

Erez Hadad and Asaf Kaufman demonstrate how an adversary can purchase an enterprise IoT device, implant custom firmware backdoors or hardware Trojans, and return it for RMA.

Exploiting Internal Manufacturer Testing Environments

When returned devices are connected to internal manufacturer diagnostic labs, malicious payloads exploit trust boundaries to execute lateral movement into corporate networks.

Hardening Return Merchandise Workflows

The authors provide hardware manufacturers and enterprise organizations with diagnostic isolation protocols and firmware attestation checks for returned equipment.

talks.title: Establishing IoT Trustworthiness: Standards, Regulation, & Verification
talks.teaser: Legal and technical cybersecurity leaders explore multi-dimensional frameworks for establishing verifiable trust and safety across the global IoT ecosystem.
talks.summary:
The Challenge of Defining IoT Trustworthiness

As billions of connected devices integrate into critical societal infrastructure, establishing verified device trustworthiness requires coordinating technical security, privacy, and regulatory policies.

Multi-Dimensional Trust Frameworks

Amit Elazari, Armen Tarkhanyan, and Ria Cheruvu review emerging international standards (NIST IR 8259, EU Cybersecurity Act) establishing baseline IoT security criteria.

Technical Verification and Attestation Mechanisms

The authors explore technical mechanisms for proving device identity, firmware integrity, and cryptographic provenance throughout a product's operational lifecycle.

A Policy Roadmap for Secure IoT Ecosystems

The presentation outlines collaborative regulatory pathways to incentivize secure product development, bug bounty adoption, and transparent security labeling.

talks.title: Mind the Gap: Managing Insecurity in Enterprise IoT
talks.teaser: Cheryl Biswas explores the growing attack surface of unmanaged enterprise IoT devices, addressing shadow IT, patch lag, and asset visibility gaps.
talks.summary:
The Expanding Attack Surface of Shadow IoT

Enterprise facilities are filled with smart TVs, HVAC controllers, security cameras, and connected coffee makers deployed without IT security knowledge or oversight.

The Inherent Insecurity of Single-Purpose Hardware

Cheryl Biswas examines the structural challenges of enterprise IoT—devices designed without update mechanisms, running outdated software stacks, and rarely patched.

Analyzing Real-World Enterprise IoT Compromises

Biswas reviews high-profile breaches where attackers used unmanaged peripheral hardware (like smart fish tanks and building sensors) as initial lateral pivot points.

A Pragmatic Blueprint for Enterprise IoT Governance

The author provides security teams with practical strategies for continuous asset discovery, automated network segmentation, and vendor risk management.
